questions.question: Why should Docker containers run as a non-root user?
choices: If an attacker escapes the container, they have root access to the host machine
Root users can't access the network
Docker doesn't support root users in production
questions.explanation: Running as root is the most common Docker security mistake. If an attacker breaks out of the container, root access means they can compromise the host. Using a non-root user (like USER appuser) limits this risk.

questions.question: What is the benefit of a multi-stage Docker build?
choices: It separates build tools from the production image, reducing size and attack surface
It allows running multiple containers simultaneously
questions.explanation: Multi-stage builds compile/prepare in a 'builder' stage, then copy only the production artifacts to a slim final image. Build tools, source code, and dev dependencies stay out of the production image.

questions.question: What does the HEALTHCHECK instruction do in a Dockerfile?
choices: It runs unit tests during the build
It tells Docker/orchestrators how to verify the container is running correctly
It encrypts the container's network traffic
It automatically restarts the container every 30 seconds
questions.explanation: HEALTHCHECK defines how Docker can verify the container is healthy. Without it, orchestrators like Kubernetes can't detect a broken container and restart it, leading to silent failures.
